sentences.text: Sam has a big red hat.
The hat sat on the mat.
A cat sat on the hat!
Sam got the hat.
The cat ran.
Dan has a dog.
The dog can dig.
Dan and the dog dug in the mud.
Mom was not glad!
Dan and the dog got a bath.
I can go to the park.
You can go with me!
We can run and play.
Are you fast?
I am!
She is fast too.
We are all fast.
A bug sat on a rug.
The bug did a jig!
It hid in a mug.
Mom got the bug.
She set it on a log.
My dog is big.
He and I go to the pond.
Do you see the ducks?
I do!
We sit and look.
He is my best pal.
A green frog sat on a stump.
He saw a dragonfly zip past.
The frog jumped and snapped!
He missed.
He tried again and got it.
What a great snack!
Chad and his mom went on a big ship.
The ship had a flag.
Chad saw fish splash in the water.
Then the ship went past a whale!
Chad was so thrilled.
Jake made a cake.
He put it on a plate.
His snake Pete came close.
Pete ate a grape, not the cake!
Jake smiled and ate a huge slice.
A small crab lived by the creek.
One day, a crow dropped a stick near him.
The crab grabbed the stick and dragged it to his home.
Now he had a bridge!
Chip the chipmunk had a plan.
He checked every path for chestnuts.
He found three under a thick bush.
Chip shoved them in his cheeks and rushed home.
It rained all day.
Dean waited by the train.
The train was late!
He read his book and ate a snack.
When the train came, Dean cheered.
He had a seat by the window.
Joan found an old boat in the snow.
She loaded it with her coat and a loaf of bread.
She floated down the snowy road like it was a river!
Her goat followed behind.
The wind was unkind today.
It undid Rosa's braids.
It unzipped her backpack.
Papers flew everywhere!
Rosa was unhappy but she refilled her bag and retied her hair.
Lee lived on Beehive Street.
Each week, she would peek at the bees.
They worked as a team to feed the queen.
Lee felt proud to keep the bees safe.
In the backyard, sunflowers grew tall.
A butterfly landed on a flowerpot.
It was beautiful!
Emma set up a birdbath nearby.
Soon, dragonflies came too.
Her backyard was a little rainforest.
Maya discovered a tide pool behind the rocks.
Tiny crabs scurried across the sand.
A purple starfish clung to a stone.
She noticed the water was remarkably clear.
Maya decided to return every weekend to study the creatures.
Leo's compass vanished from his desk.
He searched his entire room.
Under the bed, he found dust bunnies.
Behind the bookshelf, he found an old photograph.
Finally, his little sister returned it with a sheepish grin.
Nora's neighbors said nothing could grow in rocky soil.
She disagreed.
She replanted seeds three times.
She was patient and responsible.
By summer, her impossible garden was full of tomatoes and peppers.
Kai thought the storm was exciting.
Thunder boomed and lightning flashed.
His dog Biscuit felt differently.
She hid under the table and whimpered.
Kai hugged her tight.
"It's okay, Biscuit.
I'll keep you safe."
Omar built a robot for the science fair.
It could sort recycling into different bins.
Paper went left, plastic went right.
The judges were impressed.
Omar won first place because his invention helped the environment.
March 14: The fog rolled in at dawn.
I lit the beacon at precisely 5:47 AM.
Three fishing boats returned safely because of the light.
Without the lighthouse, they might have crashed against the jagged rocks.
This job may be lonely, but it matters.
In 1960, a group of children in a small town were told they couldn't use the public library.
Instead of giving up, they started their own in an abandoned basement.
They collected donated books and took turns being librarian.
Within a year, their collection had grown to over 500 books.
Deserts and tundras are both extreme environments, but they differ in important ways.
Deserts are scorching hot during the day, while tundras remain frozen year-round.
However, both have one thing in common: very little rainfall.
Animals in both places have adapted in remarkable ways to survive harsh conditions.
Before the toaster was invented in 1893, people held bread over an open flame with a fork.
It was slow, dangerous, and often resulted in burnt toast.
Albert Marsh created the first electric toaster, and breakfast was never the same.
Today, over 75 million American homes have one.
Amara stared at the letter for a long time.
Her grandmother had written it years ago but Amara had never opened it.
Her hands trembled as she unfolded the paper.
"Dear Amara, if you're reading this, you're brave enough to face anything.
Love always, Grandma."
Amara smiled through her tears.
